novel_features.name: Engagement decay
novel_features.description: Find previously-active contacts who have gone dark, ranked by prior engagement intensity.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining historical engagement snapshots against the current silence window. HubSpot's filter builder is set-based, not sequence-based.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this on Monday mornings to find warm leads that cooled — the classic re-engagement list a rep would otherwise build by hand.

novel_features.name: Lifecycle stuck
novel_features.description: Surface contacts stuck in a lifecycle stage past team-median dwell time.
novel_features.rationale: Requires reconstructing stage transitions across multiple syncs and computing per-team median dwell — HubSpot only exposes the current stage and its entry timestamp.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when a sales manager asks 'who's breaching SLA?' — outliers relative to the team's own baseline, not a hardcoded threshold.

novel_features.name: Stale but valuable
novel_features.description: Find high-score, high-revenue contacts whose engagement has cooled — the VIPs going cold.
novel_features.rationale: Ranks by a composite value/recency score that HubSpot's single-column sort can't express.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when prioritizing save-the-whale outreach. Composite ranking is what makes it different from a plain filter.

novel_features.name: Source ROI
novel_features.description: Rank contact acquisition sources by realized revenue and conversion, not raw volume.
novel_features.rationale: Joins source attribution to deal/revenue properties with statistical-minimum filtering. HubSpot's source reports show counts only.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when marketing asks where to defund. Filters small-N sources so the ranking isn't dominated by noise.

novel_features.name: Score drift
novel_features.description: Find contacts whose HubSpot score dropped meaningfully over a window — leading indicator before lifecycle catches up.
novel_features.rationale: Requires snapshotting hubspotscore per sync to compute deltas. HubSpot has no native score-history view without Operations Hub Pro.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this as an early disengagement signal that beats lifecycle stage by days or weeks.

novel_features.name: Owner overload
novel_features.description: Flag sales reps carrying more active contacts than team median, weighted by lifecycle stage.
novel_features.rationale: Weighted aggregation across owners × stages × contacts vs. team median. HubSpot reporting shows flat counts only.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when balancing book-of-business across AEs — the standard manual answer is 'export to Sheets and pivot.'

novel_features.name: Silent after first touch
novel_features.description: Find contacts who engaged exactly once and then went silent — distinguish tire-kickers from genuine interest.
novel_features.rationale: Sequence-based filter (exactly one event, then nothing) that HubSpot's set-based filter builder can't express.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when triaging which one-touch contacts are worth a follow-up vs. archive.

novel_features.name: Duplicate suspects
novel_features.description: Surface likely duplicate contacts via fuzzy match on email-local-part, normalized name, and company.
novel_features.rationale: HubSpot native dedupe is exact-email only. Pairwise similarity is computable in SQL with blocking heuristics; not in the HubSpot UI.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this during quarterly CRM hygiene. Outputs pair candidates with scores; merge stays manual (write scope intentionally out).

novel_features.name: Daily digest
novel_features.description: One-command morning briefing — new high-score contacts, biggest score drops, lifecycle promotions, freshly stale VIPs.
novel_features.rationale: Diffs snapshots across multiple dimensions — HubSpot's email digests don't cover score/stage deltas.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this on Monday morning as the single command a sales manager runs with coffee.

narrative.headline: Read-only contact analytics for HubSpot CRM — score drift, engagement decay, source ROI, and a daily digest, with a local store no other HubSpot tool ships.
narrative.value_prop: Every existing HubSpot CLI is CMS dev tooling or generic CRUD; every HubSpot MCP is conversational and write-heavy. This CLI mirrors the CRM Contacts API as typed commands, then layers nine cross-time analytics commands on top of a local SQLite store: engagement-decay, lifecycle-stuck, stale-but-valuable, source-roi, score-drift, owner-overload, silent-after-first-touch, duplicate-suspects, and daily-digest.
narrative.auth_narrative: HubSpot read-only access uses a Private App access token. Create one at https://app.hubspot.com/private-apps, grant `crm.objects.contacts.read` and `crm.schemas.contacts.read`, then export it as `HUBSPOT_PRIVATE_APP_TOKEN`. The CLI sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. No write scopes — by design.

quickstart.comment: Verify env var, token shape, and reachability without hitting paid endpoints
Incremental sync into local SQLite — pulls contacts via cursor pagination and snapshots score for trend math
Morning briefing — score deltas, lifecycle promotions, freshly stale VIPs
Re-engagement list with field projection — keeps agent context small
Channel ranking by revenue, filtered to sources with enough volume to matter

troubleshoots.fix: Re-create the Private App at https://app.hubspot.com/private-apps with `crm.objects.contacts.read` and `crm.schemas.contacts.read` scopes, then `export HUBSPOT_PRIVATE_APP_TOKEN=<new-token>`.
Run `hubspot-pp-cli sync` first — analytics commands query the local store, which is empty until the first sync completes.
HubSpot allows ~100 req/10s. The CLI backs off automatically; re-run `sync` to resume from the cursor.
score-drift needs at least two sync snapshots to compute a delta. Run `sync` twice with the desired window between runs.
Pass `--param properties=hs_email_open,hs_email_click,hs_last_activity_date` to `sync` so the local store carries the engagement fields; the default property set omits them.

Default sync doesn't return per-stage entry timestamps; lifecycle-stuck approximates dwell from `createdate`. For long-lived contacts the approximation can compress true dwell relative to a stage-entered timestamp.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for hubspot-pp-cli when the task is read-only contact analytics — re-engagement lists, lifecycle SLA breach detection, owner workload balancing, source ROI ranking, score-trend monitoring, or duplicate hygiene. The CLI works offline against a local SQLite store synced from the live API, so cross-time and composite-rank questions land in milliseconds.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for create/update/delete on contacts; scopes are read-only by design and write workflows belong in HubSpot's UI or workflows.

Do not use this CLI for Companies, Deals, Tickets, or Engagements — only Contacts. Those surfaces are out of scope for this CLI. Use a future HubSpot CLI variant once those catalog entries are available.
Do not use this CLI for HubSpot CMS, themes, or developer tooling; HubSpot's own `hubspot-cli` is the right tool there.
Do not use this CLI as a backup/export tool for compliance evidence — sync is incremental and the local store reflects whatever you last pulled.

Do not call `crm post/patch/delete-*` write commands; they exist for spec completeness but the recommended Private App scopes (`crm.objects.contacts.read`, `crm.schemas.contacts.read`) block them with HTTP 403.

recipes.title: Morning sales-manager digest
recipes.explanation: One command, three sections of cross-time deltas. Use `--select` so the response stays small enough to thread through an agent.

recipes.title: Find dark VIPs
recipes.explanation: Composite rank by value × silence. Pair with `engagement-decay` to triangulate which save-the-whale candidates deserve outreach this week.

recipes.title: Channel ROI without small-N noise
recipes.explanation: Joins source attribution to deal revenue, filters sources below the volume threshold so noisy 2-contact channels can't dominate.

recipes.title: Owner load sanity check
recipes.explanation: Weighted by lifecycle stage so SQLs count more than Leads. Shows reps above the team median — surface for the next 1:1.

recipes.title: Dedupe candidates for hygiene sprints
recipes.explanation: Pairwise fuzzy match goes beyond HubSpot's exact-email dedupe. `--select` keeps the envelope tight.
